ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of an animal cell. Inside the cell, near the central position, there is a relatively large round purple structure, and inside it there is also a small dot of deeper purple. Around it, lines labeling different cell structures can be seen. Reasoning: The question asks what the “center” is called; according to the context of the cell diagram, the center here refers to the large purple organelle near the center of the cell, not some letter label. In an animal cell, this large central structure is usually the nucleus that stores genetic material, called the nucleus.
